fatal_errors: The proposed approximately 2000 K measurement ceiling is inadequate for the targeted refractory Ta-V-Cr-W alloy melting regime.
The response omits the central MTP-plus-free-energy-perturbation intervention and instead proposes an unrelated DSC/diffraction/CALPHAD workflow.
The claimed family-wide approximately 5% accuracy is not supported by the cited evidence.
Conventional crystalline diffraction does not by itself provide an accurate liquid volume after Bragg peaks disappear; dedicated liquid-density or total-scattering methodology is required.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the requested property set and offers a testable experimental workflow, but it does not reconstruct the target approach. It misses the DFT free-energy framework, MTP replacement of EAM, FEP replacement of thermodynamic integration, 0 GPa conditions, large-supercell sampling, and the electronic-excitation and solid-state-SRO corrections. It also provides none of the target quantitative results, including sub-0.5 meV/atom FEP agreement, approximately 80% resource savings or 20-fold acceleration, 48–57 K electronic shifts, and 2.4 meV/atom SRO stabilization. The cited papers support CALPHAD screening, phase characterization, and selected binary thermodynamic assessments only broadly; they do not validate high-temperature DSC/in-situ diffraction for all listed properties or establish 5% accuracy across HEAs. The falsification threshold is clear, but the proposed reference methods are not necessarily more accurate or independent, especially for fusion enthalpy and liquid volume.
